channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: SCO trade ministers meet in Dushanbe to discuss economic cooperation and trade
item.description: Dushanbe hosted the 25th meeting of ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities of SCO member states on September 17, 2026. Tajik Minister of Economic Development and Trade Abdurahmonzoda Safarali chaired the meeting. Discussions focused on enhancing economic cooperation, increasing mutual trade, energy security, and investment.

item.title: Ombudsman's office helps children of labor migrants resume education in Batken region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman's office intervened to ensure three children of returning labor migrants could continue their education in Kyzyl-Kiya. The children were initially denied admission to a Russian-language school due to overcrowding. The Ombudsman's office contacted local authorities, and the children were subsequently placed in another school.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet head provides apartment to family of deceased rescuer
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's cabinet, Adylbek Kasymaliev, met with the wife of deceased EMERCOM lieutenant Askar Kazybekov, who died in the line of duty. Kasymaliev expressed condolences and assured the family of state support. Kazybekov was posthumously awarded the "Erdik" medal for bravery.

item.title: Schoolboy dies after fight between students in Kyrgyzstan's Suzak district
item.description: A 10th-grade student died from injuries sustained during a conflict with 11th-grade students in Zhygach-Korgon village, Suzak district. Two teenagers, aged 17 and 18, have been detained on suspicion of inflicting grievous bodily harm. A criminal case has been initiated, and the investigation is ongoing.

item.title: CIS exchange representatives discuss development of commodity and financial markets
item.description: Representatives from CIS countries' commodity and stock exchanges met in St. Petersburg to discuss the development of exchange commodity and financial markets. Key topics included the role of exchanges in economic regulation, principles for listing goods, and mutual access to securities. Discussions also covered digital financial assets and cooperation between national exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan develops 'kamikaze' drone with 1500 km range
item.description: Uzbekistan has developed a 'kamikaze' drone capable of flying up to 1500 km, presented as an alternative to the 'Shahed' drone. The drone, belonging to a private company, debuted at a defense technology exhibition in South Africa, where Uzbekistan is the sole participant from Central Asia showcasing various military products.

item.title: Schoolboy dies in Suzak district after conflict between 10th and 11th graders
item.description: A schoolboy has died in the village of Zhygach-Korgon, Suzak district, following a conflict between 10th and 11th-grade students. The 10th-grader sustained severe injuries and died en route to the hospital. Two teenagers have been detained.

item.title: Tajikistan and LONGi Discuss Solar Power Plant Construction
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources met with representatives from China's LONGi company to discuss energy sector cooperation. Particular attention was given to attracting investments for building solar power plants in Tajikistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank to Maintain Tight Monetary Policy Until Inflation Reaches 5%
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank intends to maintain strict monetary conditions until inflation stabilizes and approaches the target of 5%. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov stated that inflation has decreased from approximately 20% in 2018 to 6.2%. The bank projects inflation to be around 6.5% by the end of 2026 and reach the 5% target next year. The main refinancing rate remains at 14%.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Considers Outsourcing Part of Foreign Reserves Management
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank plans to diversify its international reserves across asset classes, currencies, and counterparties. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov announced this at an international forum in Tashkent. As of September 1, Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves exceeded $72 billion, covering over a year of imports. The bank also increased its gold reserves by nearly 50 tons in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Tajikistan and USA discuss bilateral relations and cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's First Deputy Foreign Minister Farrukh Hamralizoda met with the US Chargé d'Affaires Carson Relitz Roker on September 17, 2026. They discussed bilateral relations, focusing on strengthening political dialogue and expanding economic and social cooperation. Investment, humanitarian collaboration, and the C5+1 format were also addressed.

item.title: Bishkek schools face teacher shortage, employing nearly 500 students
item.description: Bishkek schools have 274 vacant teaching positions, particularly in science and history. To address the shortage, the city is employing around 500 students under a dual education program and through agreements with universities. The number of vacancies was 527 at the end of the previous academic year.

item.title: Uzbek Mother and Three Children Rescued from Difficult Situation in Istanbul
item.description: An Uzbek woman and her three children, who were in a difficult situation in Turkey, were sent back to Uzbekistan on September 17 with the assistance of the Uzbek Consulate General in Istanbul. The mother had gone to Istanbul for work but became homeless and helpless with her children.

item.title: UN: World Prepares for Next Pandemic Amidst Emerging Threats
item.description: The international community is intensifying preparations for future pandemics following COVID-19, which caused over seven million deaths and impacted global health systems and economies. The UN highlights the increased relevance of global readiness due to new infectious diseases, climate crises, and conflicts.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Rail Cooperation Agreements
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport met with his South Korean counterpart to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation in the transport sector, particularly railways. Two Memoranda of Understanding were signed, focusing on railway development, technology exchange, and educational cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Fines and One-Year Ban for Educators Committing Child Abuse
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced administrative liability for educators who commit violence against children during educational processes. A new law, signed by the president, imposes fines ranging from one to five basic calculation units and a one-year ban on pedagogical activities for those found guilty of physical or psychological abuse.

item.title: Two Brothers Sentenced in Fergana for Murdering Mother and Stepfather, Attempting to Kill Third Brother
item.description: A court in Fergana has sentenced two brothers for the murder of their mother and stepfather and an attempt to kill their third brother. The elder brother received a life sentence, while the younger received 13 years. They planned to seize the mother's house and valuables.

item.title: Tajikistan's Communications Service monitors service quality in Gorno-Badakhshan
item.description: Tajikistan's Communications Service is monitoring mobile and internet service quality in Gorno-Badakhshan. Working groups are assessing network infrastructure, user satisfaction, and identifying technical issues, particularly in remote mountain areas. The report specifically examined Vanj, Ishkashim, and Shugnan districts, and the city of Khorog.

item.title: Suspect arrested in Bishkek with 1.5 kilograms of synthetic drugs
item.description: A man born in 1989 was arrested in Bishkek on suspicion of distributing drugs through 'hidden locations.' During a search of his home, law enforcement found 1.5 kilograms of synthetic drug 'Alpha-PVP' and 4 grams of hashish. Investigations are ongoing to identify potential accomplices.

item.title: Urals Oil Prices Surpass $110 Per Barrel Amid Supply Concerns
item.description: Russian Urals oil prices have exceeded $110 per barrel, reaching their highest level since April. This surge is attributed to supply worries stemming from the Middle East and reduced availability from Persian Gulf producers. Fuel premiums for deliveries to India have also climbed significantly.

item.title: 1.5 Kilograms of Synthetic Drugs Confiscated from Suspect in Bishkek
item.description: A 37-year-old man was arrested in Bishkek for allegedly distributing drugs via dead drops. Authorities seized 1.5 kilograms of Alpha-PVP and 4 grams of hashish from his residence. Investigations are ongoing to identify other potential accomplices in the illicit drug trade.

item.title: Uzbek man who fought for Russia in Ukraine sentenced to 3 years
item.description: A 25-year-old Uzbek citizen, R.B., who fought for Russia in the Ukraine war, has been sentenced to three years in prison by a court in Fergana region. He signed a contract with the Russian Armed Forces for financial reasons in November 2023. He participated in combat operations in Luhansk region and was injured by a Ukrainian drone in April 2024.

item.title: Bishkek residents protest legality of 24-story building construction near kindergarten site
item.description: Bishkek residents are in conflict over the construction of a 24-story residential complex. They claim cracks appeared in the ground near their homes after excavation began. Residents and developers have met to discuss the situation, presenting differing accounts of the events and demanding an investigation into the construction's legality.

item.title: Tajikistan and MCDF discuss investment projects for infrastructure and regional connectivity
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Minister of Economic Development met with the Director-General of the Multilateral Cooperation Center for Development Finance (MCDF) to discuss strengthening cooperation and implementing priority investment projects. Discussions focused on quality infrastructure, regional ties, green economy, renewable energy, and climate adaptation.

item.title: French Interior Ministry Representative Begins Work in Tashkent to Coordinate Regional Law Enforcement Cooperation
item.description: Cyril Gu, the representative of the French Ministry of Interior, has started his activities in Tashkent. He will be responsible for coordinating cooperation between law enforcement agencies of Central Asian countries.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Karakalpakstan for Two-Day Trip
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit the Republic of Karakalpakstan for a two-day trip. During the visit, he will review projects in industry, agriculture, education, healthcare, transport, tourism, and sports, focusing on employment and community development.

item.title: Waste-to-Energy Plant Producing 110 Million kWh to Be Built in Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: Measures have been defined to implement an investment project in Jizzakh and Sirdaryo regions to improve the ecological situation and generate electricity through waste processing. The plant will produce 110 million kWh of electricity annually and is expected to be operational by September 14, 2026.

item.title: Uzbek Youth May Find Employment in Japan Through Targeted Vocational Training
item.description: Uzbek youth may be employed in Japan as plans are underway to expand job opportunities. This initiative involves targeted placement in the Japanese labor market and encouraging participation in vocational and language training. The goal is to increase future employment prospects for young Uzbeks in Japan.

item.title: Why Uzbekistan Needs International Certified Data Processing Centers for Digital Economy
item.description: The article discusses the necessity of international certified data processing centers for Uzbekistan, particularly in the context of the digital economy. It highlights that while digital economy elements like data, clouds, algorithms, and AI may seem intangible, certified centers are crucial for their effective operation and development within the country.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Approves New Date for Presidential Elections
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh, Kyrgyzstan's parliament, has amended its regulations to set a new date for presidential elections. The vote will now occur on the fourth Wednesday of January, instead of the third Sunday in October. President Sadyr Japarov signed the amendment, aligning the parliamentary regulations with the constitutional election law.

item.title: Bishkek Waste Processing Plant's Performance Assessed by Commission
item.description: A commission, including specialists from the Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision, evaluated the Bishkek waste processing plant that generates electricity. The commission inspected the landfill and the plant's operations. Plans include a second phase to increase processing capacity to 3,000 tons of waste daily.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Iraq Discuss Agreement on International Road Transport
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Iraq are working towards an agreement on international road transport, as discussed by Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Transport and Iraq's Chargé d'Affaires. Kyrgyzstan has drafted an agreement, aiming to facilitate transport routes via Central Asian countries and address visa issues for freight carriers.

item.title: Jizzakh to generate electricity from solid waste incineration
item.description: A project in Jizzakh will produce electricity by incinerating solid municipal waste. The project company will provide an $8 million bank guarantee to ensure its obligations during construction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan National Bank reports on currency exchange rates
item.description: The Kazakh tenge and Russian ruble strengthened, reaching yearly and monthly highs. The euro and Chinese yuan depreciated, while the US dollar remained unchanged. The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan intervened by selling $220.7 million in dollars on September 6.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and US National Guard discuss cultural and youth cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Minister of Culture met with the U.S. Montana National Guard to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation. Areas of focus include youth policy, education, sports, arts, and cinema, with potential for hosting cultural and film days.

item.title: Energy from waste: How South Korea solved its food waste problem
item.description: South Korea has largely eliminated household food waste from landfills by converting it into energy. New York is currently testing this approach. The article discusses the methods used and the success of this initiative.

item.title: Drone Strike Occurs Near Polish-Ukrainian Border, Warsaw on Alert
item.description: A drone strike occurred in Ukraine's Volyn region, approximately 4 km from the Polish border, on September 17. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated the explosion happened near Dorohusk, likely targeting a gas station. Polish fighter jets were scrambled, and airports in Lublin and Rzeszow temporarily suspended operations.

item.title: EU Ambassador: Democracy is Never a Finished Product, Faces Modern Challenges
item.description: The EU Ambassador to Uzbekistan stated that democracy is fundamentally the people's power, allowing citizens to choose and replace leaders. He acknowledged the growing appeal of authoritarian models but believes people ultimately desire democratic choice, even when seeking stronger leaders. Democracy, he argued, is our natural state and inherent desire.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Launch New Agricultural Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are initiating new projects focused on agricultural innovation, investment, and training. Agreements include establishing a joint working group, developing grant projects for water-saving technologies and soil fertility, and adapting agriculture to climate change.

item.title: Samarkand hosts record-breaking 46th World Chess Olympiad
item.description: The 46th World Chess Olympiad has begun in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, with a record number of participants. Over 200 countries and nearly 2000 players are competing in 11 rounds. The opening ceremony featured a drone show, 3D mapping, and fireworks. Uzbekistan's team, seeded third, secured six victories in the first round.
